newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilders ease on new liquidity pact.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilders ease on new liquidity pact.

text.p: Overnight guilders eased on Friday on the back of an ample special advances allocation and continued pressure on rates from increased offering.
Call money was quoted at 2.75-2.87 percent bid and was changing hands at around 2.81 percent, dealers said. On Thursday, one-day guilders were still quoted at 3.00-3.12 percent bid/offer.

While speculation about a reduction in German interest rates had abated since the Bundesbank's decision to hold its repo rate steady at a fixed 3.0 percent, a cut in two weeks' time was still seen as a possibility, dealers said.
Combined with other factors such as increased offering by foreign players and a relatively ample short-term liquidity allocation, this was slightly pressuring Dutch money rates, dealers said.
The Dutch central bank earlier announced it had allocated 3.9 billion guilders to the market under a seven-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent.
Longer-dated guilders were down slightly, with three-month money bid at 3.14 percent -- down from Thursday's 3.16 percent.
The guilder was pegged at 112.485 per 100 marks at its 1215 GMT fixing on Friday, off a touch from Thursday's 112.465 fix.
